name: Cook steak consistently
blurb: Consistency, not luck: the same doneness every time, with a proper crust. It comes from dry surfaces, high heat, a thermometer and a rest.
gear: A thick steak, at least 3 cm
steps: Dry the surface thoroughly and salt it — either just before cooking, or 40 minutes ahead so the salt is reabsorbed. The window in between draws out moisture and prevents a crust.
Get the pan properly hot; the oil should shimmer and just start to smoke.
Sear undisturbed to build the crust, then flip. Frequent flipping is fine for evenness once the crust has formed.
Baste with butter, garlic and thyme in the last minute, spooning continuously.
Pull it 3 to 5 °C below your target — carryover cooking does the rest. Medium rare means pulling around 52 °C.
Rest for five to ten minutes on a rack, then slice across the grain.
tips: Guessing doneness by feel is unreliable until you have cooked hundreds. Use a thermometer and learn the correlation.
Wet steak steams instead of searing. Pat it dry, and pat it dry again.
A thin steak cannot be both crusted and rare. Buy thicker.
proof: Five steaks in a row hit your target doneness within a few degrees, each with a proper crust.
